6C.(1) An individual to whom rule 6 of these Rules applies shall be entitled to a tax credit under this rule in respect of a year of assessment. (2) The tax credit shall not exceed £300 or 2 per cent of the liability to tax

partner.

a previous spouse or civil partner whose marriage or civil partnership to the individual has been dissolved or annulled by a court of competent jurisdiction; or (c) made payments in accordance with an order of court or a separation agreement to a spouse or civil

partner from whom the individual is separated by such order or agreement, shall be entitled to claim a deduction from the amount of his assessable income of either £3,455 in the case of paragraph (a) or the amount actually paid under paragraphs (b) or (c):

Provided that– (i) where a deduction is claimed under paragraphs (b) or (c) and the payments are made by virtue of an order or an agreement, the amount of the deduction shall not exceed £3,455; and (ii) the deduction allowed under this sub-rule shall be

reduced by one twelfth for each complete calendar month that the individual is not married or in a civil partnership and resident in Gibraltar (or, in the case of an individual who has paid alimony or maintenance, who is not resident in Gibraltar) during the

year of assessment. (2) Where an individual is married or in a civil partnership at the time he claims a deduction pursuant to this rule, his spouse or civil partner shall not be allowed to make any further separate claim. Deduction for disabled individuals.

7A.(1) Save as hereinafter provided, an individual who proves to the satisfaction of the Commissioner that he is the parent of an unmarried individual who - (a) resides with that parent; (b) suffers from a specific bodily or mental disability; and (c) the Director of

Social Services confirms that, notwithstanding that the 5 year residency period may not have been satisfied, by reason of that disability the parent or individual would be eligible for a disability allowance paid for by the Government, shall be entitled to claim from the amount

(No.3) Rules 1999. (4) The Commissioner may consult either the Director of Education or the Medical Director of the Gibraltar Health Authority, as the case may require, on any matter arising out of a claim to a deduction under this rule. Deduction for children.

Pension Schemes) Regulations 2010 (SI 2010 No. 51)).
Last Update: 23 Mar 2026 Date: 01 Jul 1989

Interpretation 2 In these Regulations— “ pension rule 1 ” means pension rule 1 in section 165 of the Finance Act 2004 ; “ relevant scheme funds ” means any sums and assets held under a pension scheme— to which these Regulations apply, and which
would be subject to inheritance tax if the scheme did not meet the requirements for a qualifying non-UK pension scheme.
Scope of these Regulations 3 These Regulations apply to pension schemes which are established in a country or territory outside the United Kingdom.

Requirements for qualifying non-UK pension schemes 4 1 For the purposes of section 271A of the Inheritance Tax Act 1984 (qualifying non-UK pension scheme) a pension scheme must— a be recognised for tax purposes under the tax legislation of the country or territory in which

it is established (see regulation 5) and satisfy regulation 6; or b be established by an international organisation for the purpose of providing benefits for, or in respect of, past service as an employee of the organisation and satisfy regulation 7. 2 In this regulation
“ international organisation ” means an organisation to which section 1 of the International Organisations Act 1968 applies by virtue of an Order in Council under subsection (1) of that section.

Recognition for tax purposes 5 1 A scheme is recognised for tax purposes under the tax legislation of a country or territory in which it is established if it meets both Primary Condition 1 and Primary Condition 2 and either Condition A or Condition B.

Primary Condition 1 The scheme is open to persons resident in the country or territory in which it is established. Primary Condition 2 The scheme is established in a country or territory where there is a system of taxation of personal income under which tax

relief is available in respect of pensions and— a tax relief is not available to the member on contributions made to the scheme by the member or, if the member is an employee, by their employer, in respect of earnings to which benefits under the

scheme relate; b the scheme is liable to taxation on its income and gains and is of a kind specified in the Schedule to these Regulations; or c all or most of the benefits paid by the scheme to members who are not in serious

ill-health are subject to taxation. For the purposes of this condition “ tax relief ” includes the grant of an exemption from tax. Condition A 2 The scheme is approved or recognised by, or registered with, the relevant tax authorities as a pension scheme in

the country or territory in which it is established. Condition B 3 If no system applies for the approval or recognition by, or registration with, relevant tax authorities of pension schemes in the country or territory in which it is established— a the scheme must

be resident there; b the scheme rules must provide that at least 70% of a member's relevant scheme funds will be designated by the scheme manager for the purpose of providing the member with an income for life, or, in the case of a member

who has died, so provided immediately before the member's death; and c the pension benefits payable to the member under the scheme (and any lump sum associated with those benefits) must be payable no earlier than they would be if pension rule 1 applied.

Requirements for schemes recognised for tax purposes 6 1 This regulation is satisfied if paragraph (2), (3) or (4) applies. 2 This paragraph applies if the scheme is an occupational pension scheme and there is a body in the country or territory in which it

is established— a which regulates occupational pension schemes; and b which regulates the scheme in question. 3 This paragraph applies if the scheme is not an occupational scheme and there is a body in the country or territory in which it is established— a which

regulates pension schemes other than occupational pension schemes; and b which regulates the scheme in question. 4 This paragraph applies if neither paragraph (2) nor (3) applies by reason only that no such regulatory body exists in the country or territory and— a the scheme

is established in a member State, Norway, Iceland or Liechtenstein; or b the scheme is one where— i the scheme rules provide that at least 70% of a member's relevant scheme funds will be designated by the scheme manager for the purpose of providing the

member with an income for life, or, in the case of a member who has died, so provided immediately before the member's death, and ii the pension benefits payable to the member under the scheme (and any lump sum associated with those benefits) are payable
no earlier than they would be if pension rule 1 applied. 5 In this regulation “ occupational pension scheme ” has the meaning given by section 150(5) of the Finance Act 2004.

Requirements for schemes established by international organisations 7 This regulation is satisfied if— a the scheme rules provide that at least 70% of a member's relevant scheme funds will be designated by the scheme manager for the purpose of providing the member with an income

for life, or, in the case of a member who has died, so provided immediately before the member's death, and b the pension benefits payable to the member under the scheme (and any lump sum associated with those benefits) are payable no earlier than they
would be if pension rule 1 applied.

quotes: What is my tax return and what do I need to do? A tax return consists of two main parts: Part 1. Income declaration This is where you declare all income earned during the relevant tax year and the sources of that income. For this

return, the tax year covers the period 1 July 2025 to 30 June 2026. Part 2. Claim for allowances This section is where you confirm which tax allowances you are entitled to and wish to claim. Most allowances are available under the Allowances Based System

(ABS), although some may also be available under the Gross Income Based System (GIBS). As a taxpayer, you may elect to be assessed under either system. However, regardless of your choice, the Income Tax Office will assess you under the system that results in the

lowest tax liability. For this reason, it is essential that you provide full and accurate information. Failure to provide complete information may prevent us from applying for the most favourable assessment and could result in you paying more tax than necessary. If you are an

employee taxed under the PAYE system, your tax return determines the allowances to be included in your tax code for the 2026/2027 tax year (1 July 2026 to 30 June 2027). If you are registered as trade income, your tax return tells us what allowances

you wish to claim in your assessment for the tax year 2025/2026, i.e. in the year from 1 July 2025 up to 30 June 2026. Please note that claiming an allowance does not guarantee it will be granted. We are required to verify eligibility and

ensure that appropriate supporting documentation has been provided Eligibility may also depend on factors such as your tax residency status in Gibraltar and whether your spouse or civil partner has opted to be taxed under the Gross Income Based System (GIBS). Note that even if

you have recently updated your tax code due to a change in circumstances, or notified the office of such a change, you must still complete the allowances section of your tax return. Return to list of key areas 1

Current Schedule 9 paragraphs 13–17 and 20 preserve continuity/references only within their stated conditions; no corresponding rewritten eligibility provision was established here. Allowances rule 24 now expressly concerns a non-resident receiving a Gibraltar-accruing pension and is not a general frontier-employee entitlement. [Archived Act, section 34(3)](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/uploads/legislations/income-tax/1952-11/1952-11o.pdf); [current Schedule 9](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/uploads/legislations/income-tax/2010-21/2010-21(23-03-26).pdf); [rule 24](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/uploads/legislations/income-tax/1992s016/1992s016(23-03-26).pdf). The interaction and exact partial-year calculation need resolution before applying full-year bands to a starter, leaver or intermittent worker. The examples below assume full-year activity.
old_paragraph_map.destination: Guide: Rates, bands and thresholds

ABS taxable income is the balance after eligible deductions; GIBS is not authority to transfer ABS allowances into a gross-income calculation. The following core amounts are supplemented by the ordinary claim methods below. Separate property-improvement/energy instruments, the legal basis of the webpage’s social-insurance deduction entries, and the stated drafting questions still prevent a claim to a complete relief schedule:

old_paragraph_map.old_text: For a full-year eligible ABS individual whose only other deduction is £3,455, the rule 16C top-up is £4,343 − £3,455 = **£888**, giving total deductions £4,343. old_paragraph_map.old_section: The base > Health-insurance deductions and family-policy restrictions
old_paragraph_map.old_text: For ABS, rule 20A permits a deduction for premiums or contributions payable during the assessment year to an insurance policy, scheme, society or fund **approved by the Commissioner for this rule**, providing health cover for the individual, spouse/civil partner or dependent children. The aggregate annual ceiling is **£5,395**. Rule 6A excludes this deduction for a GIBS elector; the separate rule 20B instead provides the GIBS health-insurance deduction, capped at **£3,000**, for the specified approved cover. These are deductions in calculating taxable income, not cash refunds or credits of those amounts. [Allowances Rules, rules 6A and 20A–20B, pages 16–17 and 30–31](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/uploads/legislations/income-tax/1992s016/1992s016(23-03-26).pdf).
old_paragraph_map.destination: Guide: The base > Health-insurance deductions and family-policy restrictions

old_paragraph_map.old_section: The base > Health-insurance deductions and family-policy restrictions
old_paragraph_map.old_text: Both rules reduce the deduction otherwise allowable by **one twelfth for each complete calendar month of non-residence**. Establish the eligible premium and cap first, then reduce that deduction; do not simply reduce the cap and leave a smaller premium unreduced. For an otherwise allowable £2,400 deduction and three complete non-resident months, the result is **£2,400 × 9/12 = £1,800**. This illustration concerns the deduction alone; the Guide's unresolved partial-year rate-band issue still prevents treating it as a complete part-year tax calculation. [Rules 20A(2) and 20B(2)](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/uploads/legislations/income-tax/1992s016/1992s016(23-03-26).pdf).
old_paragraph_map.destination: Guide: The base > Health-insurance deductions and family-policy restrictions

old_paragraph_map.old_section: The base > Health-insurance deductions and family-policy restrictions
old_paragraph_map.old_text: A spouse's or civil partner's GIBS election also requires checking rule 6B before claiming ABS health relief. Rule 6B(1) includes rule 20A in its restrictions; subsection (2) preserves specified claims for 2006/07 made and submitted by 30 June 2007. The separate exception in subsection (3) requires an otherwise eligible policy **held solely in the claimant's name and covering only that claimant**, plus the stated absence of a historic rule 20A claim by either partner in the manner described in subsection (2). A family policy is not within that self-only exception merely because one partner pays it. Retain both partners' elections, historic claims, policy ownership and covered-person details. [Rule 6B(1)–(3), pages 17–18](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/uploads/legislations/income-tax/1992s016/1992s016(23-03-26).pdf).
old_paragraph_map.destination: Guide: The base > Health-insurance deductions and family-policy restrictions

old_paragraph_map.old_section: The base > Health-insurance deductions and family-policy restrictions
old_paragraph_map.old_text: **Boundary examples:** assuming full-year eligibility and no spouse restriction, £6,000 of qualifying premiums reaches the ABS ceiling of £5,395. Separately, assume a GIBS individual's otherwise eligible health-insurance deduction is £3,000; three complete non-resident months reduce it to £2,250. These examples do not add ABS and GIBS deductions together. Keep the approval evidence, premium schedule, covered persons, residence calendar and rule 29 claim/supporting documents. The live claim channel and case-specific approval remain to be confirmed.
old_paragraph_map.destination: Guide: The base > Health-insurance deductions and family-policy restrictions

old_paragraph_map.old_section: The base > Low-income exemption and taper relief
old_paragraph_map.old_text: Rule 16E(1) says an individual with **gross assessable income of £11,450 or less is not subject to tax**. This is distinct from rule 16B's allowance deducted from income. Above that exemption threshold, rule 16E prescribes reductions of assessed tax in four specific ranges; it does not provide a single continuous taper covering every amount up to £19,924. [Allowances Rules, rule 16E](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/uploads/legislations/income-tax/1992s016/1992s016(23-03-26).pdf).
old_paragraph_map.destination: Guide: The base > Low-income exemption and taper relief

old_paragraph_map.old_section: The base > Low-income exemption and taper relief
old_paragraph_map.destination: Guide: The base > Low-income exemption and taper relief

old_paragraph_map.old_section: The base > Low-income exemption and taper relief
old_paragraph_map.old_text: Within the applicable range, reduced taper relief is **T0 − 0.2 × (I − L)**. Deduct the resulting relief from the assessed liability, not from income. Do not fill gaps between these ranges with an invented formula or round a boundary into a different range. The statute supplies whole-pound L values; fractional-pound boundary treatment and interaction with the Commissioner's tables require confirmation for a final assessment. [Rule 16E(2)–(4)](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/uploads/legislations/income-tax/1992s016/1992s016(23-03-26).pdf).
old_paragraph_map.destination: Guide: The base > Low-income exemption and taper relief

old_paragraph_map.old_section: The base > Low-income exemption and taper relief
old_paragraph_map.old_text: For example, at gross assessable income £17,601, relief is £64.40 − 20% × £100 = **£44.40**. At the stated upper endpoint £17,822, the formula gives **£0.20**. At £17,823 that range no longer applies; do not continue it to produce negative relief. These are relief amounts, not the person's entire tax bill.
old_paragraph_map.destination: Guide: The base > Low-income exemption and taper relief

old_paragraph_map.old_section: The base > Low-income exemption and taper relief
old_paragraph_map.old_text: Rule 16F separately specifies high-income taper relief for gross assessable income **>£99,999 and ≤£103,333**, using **£1,000 − 0.3 × (I − £100,000)**. It reduces assessed liability; it is not a new marginal tax band. At £101,000 the formula gives £700. The Commissioner can issue implementation tables under both rules. This Guide has not verified the complete current table or every interaction with other credits. [Rule 16F](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/uploads/legislations/income-tax/1992s016/1992s016(23-03-26).pdf).
old_paragraph_map.destination: Guide: The base > Low-income exemption and taper relief

old_paragraph_map.old_section: The base > Computation working paper
old_paragraph_map.old_text:
1. Establish assessable income and classify each proposed allowance or deduction.
2. Select the correct GIBS table using assessable income. Do not treat the £25,000 switch as an additional band.
3. Apply each marginal rate only to its slice. Separately compute ABS on the reviewed taxable-income base.
4. Apply only documented credits and special adjustments after confirming eligibility. Keep a separate column for them; the examples below exclude them.
5. Compare the completed liabilities, then reconcile withholding and payments. A lower preliminary subtotal is not a final assessment.
old_paragraph_map.destination: Guide: The base > Computation working paper

old_paragraph_map.old_section: The base > Computation working paper
old_paragraph_map.old_text: **Arithmetic examples, before credits and with the stated bases:** GIBS gross/base £40,000 gives £2,720 + £1,520 + £3,750 = **£7,990**. ABS taxable base £20,000 gives £560 + £2,040 + £1,560 = **£4,160**. These use different assumed bases and are not a comparison for one taxpayer. At the GIBS switch, test £25,000 and £25,001 separately; do not smooth a discontinuity without a sourced adjustment.
old_paragraph_map.destination: Guide: The base > Computation working paper

old_paragraph_map.old_section: The base > Family, disability and other ordinary ABS deductions
old_paragraph_map.old_text: Apply the system and spouse restrictions in rules 6A–6B before this schedule. Keep the supporting claim required by rule 29. These deductions reduce income; they are not cash payments of the amounts shown. [Allowances Rules, rules 6A–6B and 29](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/uploads/legislations/income-tax/1992s016/1992s016(23-03-26).pdf).

| Claim | Amount and conditions |

For qualifying alimony, maintenance or separation payments, use the actual amount; the court-order/agreement limit is £3,455. Apply the rule's complete-month reduction and separate-claim restriction. |

old_paragraph_map.old_section: The base > Family, disability and other ordinary ABS deductions
old_paragraph_map.old_text: Rule 14 prevents claiming both rules 8 and 9 for the same child. For a child not resident in Gibraltar the child must be the claimant's own child. The child's own income must not exceed the particular deduction, excluding the specified scholarship/educational awards and employment income of a full-time student at a Commissioner-approved establishment. Multiple claimants require Commissioner apportionment within the deduction, not duplicate claims. Rule 20 reduces the deductions expressly listed there by one twelfth for each complete non-resident month; it literally refers to rule 7(2), so do not replace the separate rule 7 wording with an invented uniform rule. [Rules 7, 14 and 20](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/uploads/legislations/income-tax/1992s016/1992s016(23-03-26).pdf).
old_paragraph_map.destination: Guide: The base > Family, disability and other ordinary ABS deductions

old_paragraph_map.old_section: The base > Family, disability and other ordinary ABS deductions
old_paragraph_map.old_text: Rule 18 concerns a relative maintained at the claimant's expense who cannot maintain himself through old age/infirmity, or the specified widowed mother whether incapacitated or not. The relative's total annual income must not exceed £3,455. The deduction is £250, or £400 if the dependant is ordinarily resident in Gibraltar, reduced by income exceeding £3,090; there are at most two dependants and joint contributors apportion it by their maintenance contributions. Apply rule 20. The printed income ceiling and reduction can produce an apparent negative result in part of the non-resident range; this Guide does not invent a negative deduction or silently repair that drafting. For an otherwise eligible dependant with income £3,200, the reduction is £110: £140 from the £250 amount, or £290 from £400, before other applicable reductions. [Rule 18](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/uploads/legislations/income-tax/1992s016/1992s016(23-03-26).pdf).
old_paragraph_map.destination: Guide: The base > Family, disability and other ordinary ABS deductions

old_paragraph_map.old_section: The base > Family, disability and other ordinary ABS deductions
old_paragraph_map.old_text: Rule 16A specifies a senior-citizen deduction for a man aged at least 65 or a woman aged at least 60 during the assessment year, with a complete-month non-residence reduction. Its printed formula subtracts the two named £3,455 amounts from £12,645; it is not a general instruction to add £12,645 on top of other deductions. It retains a reference to an election under revoked rule 25. Keep that reference and the actual rule 6/7 eligibility on the working paper; the current drafting does not establish a universal minimum-deduction calculation for every unmarried or mixed-system pensioner. [Rule 16A, with rules 6A–6B and 25](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/uploads/legislations/income-tax/1992s016/1992s016(23-03-26).pdf).
old_paragraph_map.destination: Guide: The base > Family, disability and other ordinary ABS deductions

old_paragraph_map.old_section: The base > Family, disability and other ordinary ABS deductions
old_paragraph_map.old_text: Rule 16D is a separate tax credit of up to £4,000, limited to tax liability, for a person aged at least 60 with its defined earned income. Check all pension/annuity exclusions: pension or annual annuity exceeding £6,000, and the stated Commissioner-opinion tests involving capital beyond 25% and a pension/annuity over £6,000. GIBS electors are excluded; the printed revoked-rule-25 reference remains. Apply the printed complete-month residence/age conditions in rule 16D(5) and the prescribed claim; do not count the same month twice or assume a refundable balance. It does not exempt all earnings after age 60. [Rule 16D](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/uploads/legislations/income-tax/1992s016/1992s016(23-03-26).pdf).
old_paragraph_map.destination: Guide: The base > Family, disability and other ordinary ABS deductions

old_paragraph_map.old_section: The base > Life assurance and pension contributions deducted from income
old_paragraph_map.old_text: For ABS, rule 21 covers qualifying own/spouse life premiums, contributions to the approved pension/provident arrangements specified in rule 21(9), and the preserved former Social Insurance (Pensions) Fund entitlement in rule 21(10). It excludes the stated statutory/personal pension arrangements from paragraph (9), prohibits relief twice for the same amount, and provides the separate-income spouse treatment in paragraph (8). Apply the overall one-sixth assessable-income ceiling, the one-seventh ceiling for life premiums and paragraph (10) contributions, and the 7% capital-sum limit for a policy securing death benefits, excluding bonuses. Reduce the allowable deduction for complete non-resident months. Rule 6A excludes rule 21 for GIBS; rule 6B's self-only life-policy exception requires its own historical-claim conditions. Do not treat all pension products as the same deduction. [Rules 6A–6B and 21](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/uploads/legislations/income-tax/1992s016/1992s016(23-03-26).pdf).
old_paragraph_map.destination: Guide: The base > Life assurance and pension contributions deducted from income

old_paragraph_map.old_section: The base > Life assurance and pension contributions deducted from income
old_paragraph_map.old_text: Rule 21A separately allows actual contributions to a Commissioner-approved personal pension scheme or retirement annuity contract, capped at the lesser of 20% of earned assessable income and £35,000. Earned assessable income is the specified trade/professional and employment income; the rule excludes earnings from employment that provides a pension or annuity, and requires the prescribed claim. Rule 6A excludes this deduction for GIBS. An otherwise eligible ABS person with £50,000 qualifying earned income and £12,000 paid has a £10,000 cap and deduction, assuming all other conditions are met. The separate GIBS approved-pension deduction remains rule 24A's £1,500 limit. [Rules 6A, 21A and 24A](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/uploads/legislations/income-tax/1992s016/1992s016(23-03-26).pdf).
old_paragraph_map.destination: Guide: The base > Life assurance and pension contributions deducted from income

old_paragraph_map.old_section: The base > Mortgage interest and home-purchase deductions
old_paragraph_map.old_text: Rule 22 permits qualifying interest actually paid for constructing, purchasing, improving or developing a Gibraltar home occupied or to be occupied as the only/main Gibraltar residence. Check the loan's use and cost limits, lender licensed to take deposits, occupation evidence and the exclusions for specified spouse/settlor transactions and excessive prices. The ordinary limit is interest attributable to at most £350,000 aggregate loan principal, not £350,000 interest a year. The rule retains a separate transition for loans made on/before 30 June 2008; do not replace it with a new-loan calculation. A claimant can elect own, spouse/partner or 50:50 allocation under the specified conditions. Where a spouse uses GIBS, retain rule 6B(5)'s printed rule-22 reference, historical-claim condition, half-deduction and one-sixth assessable-income limits; its wording does not justify bypassing the rule 6B eligibility check. GIBS has a further £1,500 annual deduction ceiling. [Allowances Rules, rule 22(1)–(2), (7)–(10)](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/uploads/legislations/income-tax/1992s016/1992s016(23-03-26).pdf).
old_paragraph_map.destination: Guide: The base > Mortgage interest and home-purchase deductions

old_paragraph_map.old_section: The base > Mortgage interest and home-purchase deductions
old_paragraph_map.old_text: Keep the disposal and use conditions with that claim. Rule 22(2A) addresses disposal or ceasing occupation within 12 months of first claiming, with its death/continuing-spouse exception. Pre-occupation disposal under rule 22(1)(d) requires the stated replacement-home use of proceeds within 12 months, otherwise the relieved tax becomes payable within 30 days after that period. Rule 22(3) separately covers a child's home and disallows relief for a year with any occupation by someone other than the child. Garage/parking relief under rule 22(4)–(6) has its own three-year disposal and twelve-month use tests and excludes a motorcycle from the specified personal motor vehicle. The enforcement wording refers to old section 74; no current assessment deadline is inferred from that unconverted reference. [Rule 22(1)(d), (2A)–(6)](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/uploads/legislations/income-tax/1992s016/1992s016(23-03-26).pdf).
old_paragraph_map.destination: Guide: The base > Mortgage interest and home-purchase deductions

old_paragraph_map.old_section: The base > Mortgage interest and home-purchase deductions
old_paragraph_map.old_text: The Home Purchase (Deductions) Rules give the post-1 July 2019 ordinary aggregate limit of £13,000 under rule 2 (own home) or 2A (child's home), subject to their separate ordinary-residence, acquisition/construction, cost/payment and Crown-property exclusions. The own-home rule excludes its specified special-status certificate holder. This is not a fresh annual allowance or an automatic allowance for each new property: apply the one-claim/one-dwelling rules, the historical pre-July-2001 adjustment, joint-owner interest reduction and elected own/spouse/50:50 allocation. Exclude the specified life-policy realisation proceeds. Rule 3 carries an unused entitlement balance to later years; rule 5's provisional tax refund is discretionary and assessment-adjustable. [Home Purchase Rules, rules 2–5](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/legislations/home-purchase-deductions-rules-1989-398/download).
old_paragraph_map.destination: Guide: The base > Mortgage interest and home-purchase deductions

old_paragraph_map.old_section: The base > Mortgage interest and home-purchase deductions
old_paragraph_map.old_text: For a current eligible GIBS claimant the post-1 July 2019 limit is £7,500 under rule 8(4), with the other restrictions intact. Where either partner uses GIBS, check the historical-claim and half-deduction provisions in rule 8(2)–(3); do not grant two full allowances. Rule 6 separately withdraws entitlement for the specified disposal or cessation of residential use within twelve months of obtaining the legal estate, subject to its death/continuing-occupation exceptions. It retains an old-section-74 assessment reference; do not infer a new assessment clock. [Home Purchase Rules, rules 6 and 8](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/legislations/home-purchase-deductions-rules-1989-398/download).
old_paragraph_map.destination: Guide: The base > Mortgage interest and home-purchase deductions

old_paragraph_map.old_section: The base > Mortgage interest and home-purchase deductions
old_paragraph_map.old_text: The separate Home Purchase (Special Deduction) Rules specify £4,000 total with at most £1,000 in any assessment year. Their rule 2 requires entitlement under the ordinary own-home rule 2; rule 3 also limits payment dates, repeat/property claims, spouse allocations and joint ownership. Rule 3(2)(f)–(g) retains the historical £10,000/£11,500 entitlement tests; the current text does not explain their application to a new £13,000 entitlement. Rule 4 excludes a GIBS elector and separately addresses a spouse's GIBS election, historical claims and half relief. Keep these unresolved eligibility conditions explicit instead of automatically adding £1,000 to every new purchaser's calculation. [Special Deduction Rules, rules 2–4](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/legislations/home-purchase-special-deduction-rules-2004-412/download).
old_paragraph_map.destination: Guide: The base > Mortgage interest and home-purchase deductions

old_paragraph_map.old_section: The base > Mortgage interest and home-purchase deductions
old_paragraph_map.old_text: For administration, the current Income Tax Office PAYE page requests the Mortgage Interest and House Purchase Allowance application, property deeds and mortgage facility letter; the lender's interest letter is required yearly. The published webpage's plain-language summary does not replace the statutory principal cap, allocation, historical conditions or forfeiture tests above. [ITO property-allowance instructions](https://www.gibraltar.gov.gi/income-tax-office/individuals-and-employees/paye).
old_paragraph_map.destination: Guide: The base > Mortgage interest and home-purchase deductions

old_paragraph_map.old_section: The base > Gym/personal-training and private-school tax credits
old_paragraph_map.old_text: Schedule 3 paragraph 19A permits a credit capped at the lower of 10% of the individual's qualifying Gibraltar gym/fitness membership or contracted Gibraltar personal-trainer cost and that individual's tax liability. A personal trainer must be registered with ITO and compliant to the Commissioner's satisfaction. The claim needs evidence for the entire cost. Unused credit becomes zero and cannot be transferred or carried forward. [Income Tax Act, Schedule 3 paragraph 19A](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/uploads/legislations/income-tax/2010-21/2010-21(23-03-26).pdf).
old_paragraph_map.destination: Guide: The base > Gym/personal-training and private-school tax credits

old_paragraph_map.old_section: The base > Gym/personal-training and private-school tax credits
old_paragraph_map.old_text: Paragraph 19B applies the same 10%-of-cost and tax-liability ceilings to a parent's private primary/secondary school tuition fees paid in Gibraltar for the defined child. Nursery is excluded from this school definition; its separate allowance has different conditions. The entire tuition cost needs supporting evidence. Unused credit becomes zero and cannot be transferred or carried forward. In separate assumed cases, £900 of qualifying gym cost with £50 liability permits £50 credit; £8,000 tuition with £900 liability permits £800. These are independent illustrations, not permission to apply several credits repeatedly against the same liability or an asserted statutory ordering between them. [Schedule 3 paragraph 19B](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/uploads/legislations/income-tax/2010-21/2010-21(23-03-26).pdf).
old_paragraph_map.destination: Guide: The base > Gym/personal-training and private-school tax credits

old_paragraph_map.old_section: The base > Approved pensions and imported-pension exceptions
old_paragraph_map.old_text: Rule 3A covers pensions from a statutory scheme or provident/other fund approved by the Commissioner where the individual is **60 or over**, or meets one of the specified earlier-retirement categories. Those include the stated compulsory Pensions Act retirement, Royal Gibraltar Regiment retirement at 55 or over, and listed customs, port, fire/rescue and defence-police retirements between 55 and 60. Do not turn the list into an exemption for every retired person aged 55. [Rule 3A(1)](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/uploads/legislations/income-tax/1992s016/1992s016(23-03-26).pdf).
old_paragraph_map.destination: Guide: The base > Approved pensions and imported-pension exceptions

old_paragraph_map.old_section: The base > Approved pensions and imported-pension exceptions
old_paragraph_map.old_text: Qualifying pension income is taxed at **0%**, subject to the section 14A exception. Other chargeable income remains separately taxable under the prescribed bands after applicable apportioned allowances/deductions. The pension rule does not exempt rental, trading or employment income merely because its recipient is retired. Verify the fund approval and individual category, not just the payer's description of the transfer. [Rule 3A(2)–(3)](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/uploads/legislations/income-tax/1992s016/1992s016(23-03-26).pdf).
old_paragraph_map.destination: Guide: The base > Approved pensions and imported-pension exceptions

old_paragraph_map.old_section: The base > Approved pensions and imported-pension exceptions
old_paragraph_map.old_text: Section 14A instead taxes its specified imported-pension income at **2.5% insofar as it forms part of taxable income**, notwithstanding contrary provisions of the Act/allowance rules. The source must be a Commissioner-approved fund receiving the relevant funds or benefit entitlement transferred from the specified overseas pension scheme. Although subsection (2) uses European Union terminology, subsection (5) expressly defines it for this section as **the United Kingdom**. Do not extend this rule to every EU or foreign pension from the heading alone. [Section 14A(1)–(2), (5)](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/uploads/legislations/income-tax/2010-21/2010-21(23-03-26).pdf).
old_paragraph_map.destination: Guide: The base > Approved pensions and imported-pension exceptions

old_paragraph_map.old_section: The base > Approved pensions and imported-pension exceptions
old_paragraph_map.old_text: Approval requires irrevocably binding fund rules restricting commutation to **30%** of the relevant assets, subject to a higher/lower percentage set by the Commissioner having regard to origin-country law; preventing benefits before **55** except qualifying ill-health retirement; and restricting onward transfers to approved funds or funds containing equivalent irrevocable provisions. For ill health, the administrator needs registered-medical-practitioner evidence of inability to carry on the occupation through mental or physical illness. These are Gibraltar approval conditions, not certification of UK transfer eligibility or freedom from UK charges. [Section 14A(3)–(4)](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/uploads/legislations/income-tax/2010-21/2010-21(23-03-26).pdf).
old_paragraph_map.destination: Guide: The base > Approved pensions and imported-pension exceptions

old_paragraph_map.old_section: The base > Approved pensions and imported-pension exceptions
old_paragraph_map.old_text: Section 14B provides a separate 2.5% route for an approved fund conforming to the UK statutory instrument made under section 271A of the Inheritance Tax Act 1984, with its own stated fund restrictions. The referenced instrument is the **Inheritance Tax (Qualifying Non-UK Pension Schemes) Regulations 2010, SI 2010/51**: the official revised text and HMRC IHTM17025 identify its requirements. Identification of that instrument does not establish any particular fund's conformity or Gibraltar approval. [Section 14B(1)–(5)](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/uploads/legislations/income-tax/2010-21/2010-21(23-03-26).pdf).
old_paragraph_map.destination: Guide: The base > Approved pensions and imported-pension exceptions

old_paragraph_map.old_section: The base > Section 14B: evidence for the UK scheme requirements
old_paragraph_map.old_text: Use the [revised SI 2010/51](https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2010/51) when checking the cross-reference. The original 2010 PDF is an as-made text; the retrieved revised XML records a version effective from 31 December 2020. [HMRC IHTM17025](https://www.gov.uk/hmrc-internal-manuals/inheritance-tax-manual/ihtm17025) also identifies SI 2010/51 as the regulations under section 271A. This Guide checks the instrument's qualification structure, not a fund's status or UK inheritance-tax liability.
old_paragraph_map.destination: Guide: The base > Section 14B: evidence for the UK scheme requirements

old_paragraph_map.old_section: The base > Section 14B: evidence for the UK scheme requirements
old_paragraph_map.old_text: Regulation 4 provides two routes. The ordinary route requires **both** tax recognition under regulation 5 and compliance with regulation 6. The international-organisation route requires an organisation within regulation 4(2), a scheme for benefits relating to past employment with that organisation, and regulation 7. Do not replace the ordinary route with a general assertion that the scheme is regulated. [Regulations 3–4](https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2010/51/regulation/4).
old_paragraph_map.destination: Guide: The base > Section 14B: evidence for the UK scheme requirements

old_paragraph_map.old_section: The base > Section 14B: evidence for the UK scheme requirements
old_paragraph_map.old_text: For the ordinary route, prepare an evidence schedule:

old_paragraph_map.old_text:
| Test | Evidence and conditions |

old_paragraph_map.old_text: Source: [regulations 5–6 and Schedule](https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2010/51). The Schedule's specified scheme is an Australian complying superannuation plan as defined there; the taxable-income/gains alternative is not open to every taxed pension fund. Regulation 7 separately imposes the 70% lifetime-income and pension-rule-1 timing requirements on the international-organisation route. [Regulation 7](https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2010/51/regulation/7).

old_paragraph_map.old_section: The base > Section 14B: evidence for the UK scheme requirements
old_paragraph_map.old_text: The **70% test is route-specific**, rather than a universal stand-alone certification of QNUPS status. It uses “relevant scheme funds” as defined in regulation 2, not automatically every asset in a member's pension portfolio. Where pension rule 1 is incorporated, verify its applicable version and any relevant protection before selecting a benefit date; Gibraltar's domestic age-55 condition alone does not resolve that UK cross-reference. Keep the scheme's establishment, tax recognition, regulation, rules and chosen statutory route on file. old_paragraph_map.old_text: **Computation example:** assume an individual's established taxable amount within section 14A is £20,000. Tax on that component is **£20,000 × 2.5% = £500**. If a different £20,000 pension satisfies rule 3A and is outside the overriding imported-pension provisions, its rule 3A tax is £0. These are alternative classifications; the taxpayer cannot elect the cheaper result simply by describing the same pension differently. Neither figure is the person's total tax bill.

old_paragraph_map.old_section: The base > Section 14B: evidence for the UK scheme requirements

old_paragraph_map.old_section: The base > Death during the tax year
old_paragraph_map.old_text: Section 47 transfers the deceased individual's rights, duties and tax liabilities concerning **income arising before death** to the executor, subject to its assessment limit. Tax payable by the executor under that section is a debt payable out of the deceased's estate. The section does not by itself classify income arising to the estate after death or establish inheritance-tax treatment. Separate pre-death income from later estate income and retain the executor's authority. [Section 47(1)](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/uploads/legislations/income-tax/2010-21/2010-21(23-03-26).pdf).
old_paragraph_map.destination: Guide: The base > Death during the tax year

old_paragraph_map.old_section: The base > Death during the tax year
old_paragraph_map.old_text: An assessment or additional assessment on that pre-death income must not be made later than the **end of the third year of assessment following the year in which death occurred**. This is not a three-year anniversary measured from the death date, nor a three-year extension for submitting every return. Keep ordinary return, payment, appeal and refund deadlines separately. [Section 47(2)](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/uploads/legislations/income-tax/2010-21/2010-21(23-03-26).pdf).
old_paragraph_map.destination: Guide: The base > Death during the tax year

old_paragraph_map.old_section: The base > Death during the tax year
old_paragraph_map.old_text: **Assessment-period example:** a death on 15 October 2026 falls in the year ending 30 June 2027. The three following years end on 30 June 2028, 2029 and 2030, so the section 47(2) endpoint is **30 June 2030**. This does not say that an existing tax debt disappears on that date or that no return is required until then.
old_paragraph_map.destination: Guide: The base > Death during the tax year

old_paragraph_map.old_section: The base > Death during the tax year
old_paragraph_map.old_text: Section 47(3) reduces deductions allowable under **rules 6–19** of the Income Tax (Allowances, Deductions and Exemptions) Rules 1992 by **one twelfth for each complete calendar month** by which death precedes the assessment-year end. Check the particular deduction's legal basis and eligibility first. Do not extend this specific cross-reference to every relief, calculate a daily fraction, or apply it as a reduction of gross income under both tax systems. [Section 47(3)](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/uploads/legislations/income-tax/2010-21/2010-21(23-03-26).pdf).
old_paragraph_map.destination: Guide: The base > Death during the tax year

old_paragraph_map.old_section: The base > Death during the tax year
old_paragraph_map.old_text: **Allowance example:** assume a deduction within that rule range has an otherwise established annual amount of £6,000. For death on 15 October in a year ending the following 30 June, November–June gives eight complete calendar months. The reduction is **£6,000 × 8/12 = £4,000**, leaving **£2,000**. For death on 15 June, there are no complete calendar months before 30 June and this particular reduction is zero. The £6,000 is an illustrative input, not a published allowance amount.
old_paragraph_map.destination: Guide: The base > Death during the tax year

old_paragraph_map.old_section: The base > Death during the tax year
old_paragraph_map.old_text: Recommended records: death date, executor authority, income cut-off, year-by-year assessments/payments, each deduction's governing rule and complete-month computation. Notification and final-return channels, post-death estate income and treatment of each specialised deduction still require verification. See [assessment appeals and refund claims](gi-income-tax-assessment-appeals.md) for the separate procedural clocks; no estate-wide tax clearance is established by this section.
old_paragraph_map.destination: Guide: The base > Death during the tax year

old_paragraph_map.old_section: Deadlines and filing
old_paragraph_map.old_text: Section 28(1) requires a full return by **30 November immediately following the assessment-year end**, subject to its exceptions. For the year ending 30 June 2027 this gives 30 November 2027, unless an applicable legal change or authorised extension alters it. Section 28(2)'s exclusion for foreign income relieved to nil requires the Commissioner's discretionary confirmation; a taxpayer cannot simply omit the income on that assumption. [Income Tax Act, section 28](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/uploads/legislations/income-tax/2010-21/2010-21(23-03-26).pdf).
old_paragraph_map.destination: Guide: Deadlines and filing

old_paragraph_map.old_section: Deadlines and filing > Payments on account and the balance
old_paragraph_map.old_text: For individuals, section 39(2) bases two instalments on **50% each of the preceding assessment year's relevant tax liability**. The relevant income is Schedule 1 Table A paragraph 2 (property income) and Table B paragraph 2 (trade/business/profession/vocation income). For this calculation, the listed income is treated as charged after income subject to PAYE withholding. Do not automatically take 50% of a mixed-income taxpayer's entire prior-year tax bill. [Income Tax Act, section 39(2); Schedule 1](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/uploads/legislations/income-tax/2010-21/2010-21(23-03-26).pdf).
old_paragraph_map.destination: Guide: Deadlines and filing > Payments on account and the balance

old_paragraph_map.old_section: Deadlines and filing > Payments on account and the balance
old_paragraph_map.old_text: The instalments fall due on **31 January and 30 June within the assessment year** and are credited against the return liability. For 1 July 2026–30 June 2027, those dates are **31 January 2027 and 30 June 2027**. Section 39(1) supplies the general November payment rule, subject to its exceptions; the Income Tax Office explains that self-employed taxpayers pay the remaining balance when submitting the return, no later than **30 November**. For this year the balance deadline is therefore **30 November 2027**. A weekend adjustment is not assumed here. [Section 39(1)–(3)](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/uploads/legislations/income-tax/2010-21/2010-21(23-03-26).pdf); [Income Tax Office payment guidance](https://www.gibraltar.gov.gi/income-tax-office/individuals-and-employees/self-employed).
old_paragraph_map.destination: Guide: Deadlines and filing > Payments on account and the balance

old_paragraph_map.old_section: Deadlines and filing > Payments on account and the balance
old_paragraph_map.old_text: A taxpayer expecting the required instalments to exceed the current year's liability can apply for full or partial discharge under section 39(5). The Commissioner decides under subsection (6); an application is not itself an approved reduction. Subsection (7) applies surcharges to unpaid instalments and treats a subsequently established shortfall after a reduction claim as due on the original instalment date. Keep the claim, calculation, decision and actual payments. [Section 39(5)–(7)](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/uploads/legislations/income-tax/2010-21/2010-21(23-03-26).pdf).
old_paragraph_map.destination: Guide: Deadlines and filing > Payments on account and the balance

old_paragraph_map.old_section: Deadlines and filing > Payments on account and the balance
old_paragraph_map.old_text: **Instalment example:** assume the correctly identified preceding-year relevant liability is £6,000, with no approved reduction. Each instalment is £3,000. If final current-year liability is £7,500 and both instalments were paid, the remaining balance is **£1,500**. If final liability instead is £5,000, payments exceed it by **£1,000**, to be reconciled as a repayment position; this is not an extra negative payment instalment. Assume no other withholding, credit, surcharge or offset in either illustration.
old_paragraph_map.destination: Guide: Deadlines and filing > Payments on account and the balance

old_paragraph_map.old_section: Deadlines and filing > Payments on account and the balance
old_paragraph_map.old_text: The authenticated 2026/27 return fields/release and special assessment payment cases remain to be verified; the published ordinary service and departure routes are recorded below. Keep return delivery, individual tax payments and employer PAYE remittances separate. See the [payroll Guide](gi-payroll-social-insurance.md) for employer reporting. The self-employed webpage labels its allowance table 2021/22 and 2022/23; that table is not used here to establish current allowance figures.
old_paragraph_map.destination: Guide: Deadlines and filing > Payments on account and the balance

old_paragraph_map.old_section: Deadlines and filing > Published return, payment and departure routes
old_paragraph_map.old_text: The current government Tax eServices page lists separate “Tax return”, “Pay income tax online” and “Represent or authorise another individual” services. Its return/representation entry requires registration of a personal account, identity verification and registration for tax eServices, with the taxpayer-reference linking step. Establish the taxpayer and representative authority first; keep the submitted year, declaration/claim attachments, receipt, payment reference and payment reconciliation separately. This public listing verifies published routes. It does not show that the future 2026/27 return is already released, reveal authenticated fields, or prove a return/payment was accepted. The statutory filing/payment dates above still control their respective obligations. [Government Tax eServices](https://portal.egov.gi/services/tax).
old_paragraph_map.destination: Guide: Deadlines and filing > Published return, payment and departure routes

old_paragraph_map.old_section: Deadlines and filing > Published return, payment and departure routes
old_paragraph_map.old_text: As read on 28 October 2026, the ITO main page and current return guidance say Tax eService is temporarily unavailable and direct taxpayers to the editable PDF return by email; the public service listing above does not establish availability. The current IT1 covers income and outgoings for 1 July 2025–30 June 2026, with its separate election/allowance part labelled PAYE/HEPSS for the year commencing 1 July 2026 and Other for the year ending 30 June 2026, and a stated receipt deadline of 30 November 2026. Its first-page routing table gives PAYE returns to **paye.returns@gibraltar.gov.gi**, Other returns to **taxopi@gibraltar.gov.gi**, and HEPSS returns to **taxqi@gibraltar.gov.gi**. It requires photo ID, says no taxpayer signature is needed, and rejects a return without ID. A representative supplies authority and name/capacity. The guidance recommends PDF, JPEG or PNG attachments and says paper/lobby-mailbox returns are not accepted. These are the published 2026 filing arrangements, not verified delivery receipts or an assertion that the future year-ending-June-2027 return is released. Follow the actual form year/type and retain submission and assessment evidence. [ITO notice](https://www.gibraltar.gov.gi/income-tax-office); [IT1 first page](https://www.gibraltar.gov.gi/uploads/Income%20Tax%20Office/Employers/Tax_ReturnForm2026.pdf); [return guidance, opening notice and pages 3, 10–12](https://www.gibraltar.gov.gi/uploads/Income%20Tax%20Office/Tax%20Returns/Tax%20Return%20Guidance%202026_.pdf).
old_paragraph_map.destination: Guide: Deadlines and filing > Published return, payment and departure routes

old_paragraph_map.old_section: Deadlines and filing > Published return, payment and departure routes
old_paragraph_map.old_text: For an employee leaving Gibraltar permanently or indefinitely, the current ITO PAYE FAQ instructs submission of the Claim for Final Assessment form with Part 1 of the last employer's P7A to **paye.leavinggib@gibraltar.gov.gi**. Keep employment-end and departure dates, income/benefits, claims, withholding and the resulting assessment/payment evidence. The FAQ supplies a published claim route, not a universal departure-tax exemption, a cancellation of an existing debt, or a replacement for the applicable statutory return/payment clock. No form has been submitted or tax paid in preparing this Guide. [ITO departure instructions](https://www.gibraltar.gov.gi/income-tax-office/individuals-and-employees/paye).
old_paragraph_map.destination: Guide: Deadlines and filing > Published return, payment and departure routes

old_paragraph_map.old_section: Penalties and interest
old_paragraph_map.old_text: For failure to complete and deliver a section 28 return, section 65 provides **£50**, a further **£300** if failure continues after three months beginning with the filing date, and another **£500** after six months. All three amount to **£850**, not £500 total. The Commissioner can set aside one or more penalties if satisfied a reasonable excuse existed throughout the default; relief is not automatic. [Section 65(1), (2), (4)–(5)](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/uploads/legislations/income-tax/2010-21/2010-21(23-03-26).pdf).
old_paragraph_map.destination: Guide: Penalties and interest

old_paragraph_map.old_section: Penalties and interest
old_paragraph_map.old_text: Section 64 imposes a **10%** surcharge on tax unpaid on the day after its due date. If the tax and first surcharge remain unpaid at the statutory 90-day point, a further **20% of the outstanding tax and surcharge** becomes due. With £1,000 wholly unpaid throughout, the first surcharge is £100, then £220, leaving **£1,320**; it is not a flat 30% addition to principal. Establish the actual payment due date and any payments before using this example. Appeal/postponement rules are addressed in the [assessment and appeals Guide](gi-income-tax-assessment-appeals.md). [Section 64](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/uploads/legislations/income-tax/2010-21/2010-21(23-03-26).pdf).
old_paragraph_map.destination: Guide: Penalties and interest

old_paragraph_map.old_section: Penalties and interest
old_paragraph_map.old_text: These are return and payment provisions, not an exhaustive account of incorrect-return, notice, fraud or criminal penalties. No interest rate is asserted here.
old_paragraph_map.destination: Guide: Penalties and interest

old_paragraph_map.old_section: Cross-border points
old_paragraph_map.old_text: Ordinary residence, source of income and treaty residence are separate determinations. Rule 3 generally specifies **17% on the first £16,000 of taxable income and 39% on the remainder** for non-resident individuals, subject to GIBS and its express exclusions. It excludes persons covered by Allowances Rules 24(1), which concerns non-residents receiving a Gibraltar-accruing pension. Rule 24(2)–(3) limits that relief by reference to total worldwide income and specifies treatment of foreign-tax relief. Do not apply the ordinary resident ABS table or full personal allowances to every frontier worker. [Rates Rules, rule 3](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/uploads/legislations/income-tax/1989s096/1989s096(01-07-24).pdf); [Allowances Rules, rule 24](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/uploads/legislations/income-tax/1992s016/1992s016(23-03-26).pdf).
old_paragraph_map.destination: Guide: Cross-border points

old_paragraph_map.old_section: Cross-border points
old_paragraph_map.old_text: Treaty eligibility, pension exemptions, employment-location allocation and foreign relief require separate conclusions; see the [foreign-tax relief Guide](gi-foreign-tax-relief.md). These rules alone do not resolve a Spain–Gibraltar residence case.
old_paragraph_map.destination: Guide: Cross-border points

old_paragraph_map.old_section: Cross-border points > Non-resident pensioner relief: worldwide-income limit
old_paragraph_map.old_text: Rule 24(1) permits a **non-resident individual receiving a pension accruing in Gibraltar** to claim the deductions, allowances and reliefs in rules 6–21 as if resident throughout the assessment year, subject to the Rules and the limit below. It does not grant that treatment to every non-resident employee or make a pension taxable where an exemption or treaty excludes it. Establish pension source, chargeability, system eligibility and each relief's conditions before applying the limit. [Allowances Rules, rule 24(1)](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/uploads/legislations/income-tax/1992s016/1992s016(23-03-26).pdf).
old_paragraph_map.destination: Guide: Cross-border points > Non-resident pensioner relief: worldwide-income limit

old_paragraph_map.old_section: Cross-border points > Non-resident pensioner relief: worldwide-income limit
old_paragraph_map.old_text: For the rule 24(2) comparison, record **W**, total income from all sources including income outside Gibraltar's tax charge; **G**, income subject to the Gibraltar tax charge; and **H**, the hypothetical tax if total worldwide income were chargeable. The permitted relief cannot reduce the amount payable below **H × G / W**. Compute both actual and hypothetical tax **without foreign-tax relief** for this comparison, as rule 24(3) requires. This is a restriction on the specified relief, not a separate charge on otherwise exempt foreign income. Do not use the foreign country's tax bill as H or subtract a foreign credit before testing the floor. Foreign-tax relief needs its separate legal analysis. [Rule 24(2)–(3)](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/uploads/legislations/income-tax/1992s016/1992s016(23-03-26).pdf).
old_paragraph_map.destination: Guide: Cross-border points > Non-resident pensioner relief: worldwide-income limit

old_paragraph_map.old_section: Cross-border points > Non-resident pensioner relief: worldwide-income limit
old_paragraph_map.old_text: **Illustrative comparison:** assume W = £50,000, G = £20,000 and an independently established hypothetical tax H = £10,000. The floor is £4,000. If the otherwise calculated liability after the claimed relief is £3,000, relief must be restricted by £1,000 to leave £4,000 before foreign-tax relief. If that liability is £5,000, the floor requires no adjustment. These assumed tax amounts illustrate the restriction; they are not computed liabilities for a particular pensioner, approved pension or tax system. With W = 0, do not divide by zero or invent a liability; revisit the charging and income facts.
old_paragraph_map.destination: Guide: Cross-border points > Non-resident pensioner relief: worldwide-income limit

old_paragraph_map.old_section: Cross-border points > Non-resident pensioner relief: worldwide-income limit
old_paragraph_map.old_text: Rule 29 requires a claim in a return on the proper form, or another form and manner prescribed by the Commissioner, with the particulars and supporting proof required. Record worldwide income evidence, the Gibraltar-source pension, each relief claimed, both tax computations and the separate foreign-credit analysis. A working-paper calculation is not a submitted claim; the current form, channel and any case-specific evidence request remain to be verified. [Rule 29](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/uploads/legislations/income-tax/1992s016/1992s016(23-03-26).pdf).
old_paragraph_map.destination: Guide: Cross-border points > Non-resident pensioner relief: worldwide-income limit

old_paragraph_map.old_section: Two worked examples that recompute
old_paragraph_map.old_text: **Example 1: full-year GIBS before other adjustments.** With established assessable income £40,000, the higher-income table gives £17,000 × 16% + £8,000 × 19% + £15,000 × 25% = **£7,990**. This assumes the election and full-year treatment apply; no additional deduction or credit is assumed.
old_paragraph_map.destination: Guide: Two worked examples that recompute

old_paragraph_map.old_section: Two worked examples that recompute
old_paragraph_map.old_text:
```oa-check
name: Full-year GIBS income 40000
inputs:
  income: 40000
steps:
  - first: min(income, 17000) * 0.16
  - second: min(max(income - 17000, 0), 8000) * 0.19
  - third: min(max(income - 25000, 0), 15000) * 0.25
  - fourth: min(max(income - 40000, 0), 65000) * 0.28
  - remainder: max(income - 105000, 0) * 0.25
  - tax: first + second + third + fourth + remainder
expected:
  tax: 7990
```
old_paragraph_map.destination: Guide: Two worked examples that recompute

old_paragraph_map.old_section: Two worked examples that recompute
old_paragraph_map.old_text: **Example 2: full-year ABS top-up and tax before credit.** Assume £24,343 assessable income, only the £3,455 personal deduction, full eligibility for the £888 top-up and no other deductions. Taxable income is £20,000; tax before the separately determined rule 6C credit is **£4,160**. This is a different taxpayer/base from Example 1, not an ABS-versus-GIBS comparison for one person.
old_paragraph_map.destination: Guide: Two worked examples that recompute

old_paragraph_map.old_section: Two worked examples that recompute
old_paragraph_map.old_text:
```oa-check
name: ABS minimum deduction top-up and pre-credit liability
inputs:
  assessable: 24343
  personal: 3455
  minimum_deductions: 4343
steps:
  - topup: max(0, minimum_deductions - personal)
  - taxable: max(0, assessable - personal - topup)
  - first: min(taxable, 4000) * 0.14
  - second: min(max(taxable - 4000, 0), 12000) * 0.17
  - remainder: max(taxable - 16000, 0) * 0.39
  - tax_before_credit: first + second + remainder
expected:
  topup: 888
  taxable: 20000
  tax_before_credit: 4160
```
old_paragraph_map.destination: Guide: Two worked examples that recompute

old_paragraph_map.old_section: Ask the client first
old_paragraph_map.old_text:
1. Which days were spent in Gibraltar across the relevant three years, and which complete months had no Gibraltar work/activity?
2. What income arose by category and location, and what tax was withheld or paid abroad?
3. Which system was elected by the taxpayer and spouse/civil partner, and what earlier claims or approvals exist?
4. What documents support each allowance, approved pension contribution and credit?
5. Are there special-status certificates, pensions, a return notice, an extension or an outstanding assessment?
